title: Policy-Value Identification in Confounded POMDPs with Sparsely Scheduled Proxies
banked_reason: kernel_substituted@oeq:all-strata: the original sound-complete all-rank sparse-schedule topic still leaves schedules without an initial proxy and rank-one fibers outside H=3,S={0,2} open.
gap_reasons: The note proves a full-fiber decision for rank-two initial-proxy laws and for the H=3, S={0,2} rank-one branch; its examples also establish genuine policy-value ambiguity. It does not deliver the advertised calculus for arbitrary sparse schedules: schedules without an initial proxy and rank-one non-iid laws at other horizons remain open.
The coefficient construction is sound when an exhaustive chart family is supplied, but that conditional result does not close those missing fibers.
These limits make the delivered contribution a specialized identification result rather than a field-wide calculus.
proof_attempt_summary: The run constructed a sound complete rank-two initial-proxy chart and exact policy-value decision, verified an exact singleton sparse law, and then proved an exhaustive non-iid rank-one classification for H=3,S={0,2} together with a constrained-domain secant lemma. The sole validity-gate repair therefore closed every initial-table rank at that fixed schedule, but the original field kernel required arbitrary sparse schedules. Schedules with no initial proxy, rank-one fibers at other horizons or schedules, and universal rational-witness classification remain open, so the fixed-schedule theorem could not replace the promised all-schedule calculus.
tldr: For positive binary confounded POMDPs with a shared action-neutral proxy on a sparse schedule, the exact behavior law determines some policy values even when it does not determine the latent model. When the initial proxy is measured and its \(2\)-by-\(4\) table has rank two, a proved rational two-coordinate chart covers the entire positive fiber. An exact semialgebraic test then returns the algebraic identified value or strictly positive algebraic compatible twins, including on singular and disconnected fibers. The sparse non-iid bounded test is a singleton fiber with identified values. Existing iid and one-reset charts admit polynomial coefficient certificates; structural coverage of the remaining rank strata remains open.
gap: Positive Mealy equivalence and proximal POMDP bridge formulas address behavior realization or sufficient identification regimes, but do not supply a component-complete causal action/reward/proxy fiber test for this finite sparse class.
fill: Prove exhaustive positive causal charts or exceptional-piece coverage over observable rank strata, beginning with the bounded outside-chart component test, then apply conditional coefficient certificates; if this fails, identify the obstruction and state the strongest valid replacement.
